stemText: According to Werner's coordination theory, which of the following statements regarding the primary and secondary valencies of a central metal ion is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Primary valencies are non-ionizable and directional, whereas secondary valencies are ionizable and non-directional.

options.label: B
options.text: Primary valencies are ionizable and satisfied by negative ions, whereas secondary valencies are non-ionizable, directional, and satisfied by neutral molecules or negative ions.

options.label: C
options.text: Primary valencies are satisfied only by neutral molecules, whereas secondary valencies are satisfied only by negative ions.

options.label: D
options.text: Both primary and secondary valencies determine the stereochemistry and spatial geometry of the complex.

solution.explanationText: Werner's coordination theory postulates that transition metals exhibit two types of valencies: (1) Primary valency, which corresponds to the oxidation state of the metal; it is ionizable, non-directional, and satisfied exclusively by negative ions. (2) Secondary valency, which corresponds to the coordination number; it is non-ionizable, directional in space, and satisfied by negative ions or neutral donor molecules, determining the geometry of the complex.

stemText: Which of the following ligands is an ambidentate ligand capable of coordinating to a central metal atom through two different donor atoms?

solution.explanationText: An ambidentate ligand is a monodentate ligand that possesses two different donor atoms and can coordinate to a central metal atom through either one of them. The thiocyanate ion (SCN-) can coordinate via sulfur (-SCN, thiocyanato) or via nitrogen (-NCS, isothiocyanato). In contrast, oxalate and ethylenediamine are symmetrical bidentate chelating ligands.

stemText: The correct IUPAC name of the coordination compound [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 is:

solution.explanationText: Vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin) is a vital biological coordination compound containing cobalt(III) at the center of a corrin macrocyclic ring. In contrast, hemoglobin contains iron(II), chlorophyll contains magnesium(II), and carbonic anhydrase contains zinc(II).

stemText: Which of the following chemical species CANNOT act as a chelating ligand when coordinating to a single metal ion?

solution.explanationText: A chelating ligand must be a polydentate ligand possessing two or more donor atoms arranged such that they can simultaneously bind to a single central metal atom to form a ring. Ethylenediamine, dimethylglyoximato, and oxalate are bidentate ligands that form stable chelate rings. Pyridine (C5H5N) has only one nitrogen donor atom; it is strictly a monodentate ligand and cannot form a chelate ring.

stemText: Aqueous solutions of transition metal complexes often exhibit vibrant colors due to d-d electronic transitions. Which of the following complex ions is completely colorless in aqueous solution?

solution.explanationText: Color in transition metal complexes arises primarily from the promotion of an electron from lower-energy t2g orbitals to higher-energy eg orbitals (d-d transitions). For d-d transitions to occur, the d-subshell must be partially filled (d1 to d9). In [Zn(H2O)6]2+, Zn2+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d^10. Because the d-subshell is completely filled, no d-d transition is possible, rendering [Zn(H2O)6]2+ completely colorless. Ti3+ (d1), Cu2+ (d9), and Ni2+ (d8) have partially filled d-orbitals and are colored.

stemText: One mole of a cobalt(III) coordination compound with the empirical formula CoCl3 · 5NH3 is treated with excess aqueous AgNO3 solution, resulting in the instantaneous precipitation of exactly 2 moles of AgCl(s). The structural formula of the complex is:

solution.explanationText: According to Werner's theory, only the chloride ions residing outside the coordination sphere (in the ionization sphere) ionize in aqueous solution to precipitate as AgCl upon reaction with AgNO3. Because 1 mole of the complex yields exactly 2 moles of AgCl, there must be 2 chloride ions outside the brackets: [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2. The inner sphere contains one Co3+, five NH3 molecules, and one Cl- ion, satisfying the coordination number of 6.

stemText: The pair of coordination compounds [Co(NH3)5(SO4)]Br and [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 represents which type of isomerism?

solution.explanationText: Ionization isomerism occurs when a ligand inside the coordination sphere and an anion outside the coordination sphere exchange positions, giving rise to isomers that produce different ions in aqueous solution. [Co(NH3)5(SO4)]Br gives Br- ions in solution (yielding a pale yellow precipitate with AgNO3), whereas [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 gives SO4^2- ions in solution (yielding a white precipitate with BaCl2).

stemText: Which of the following coordination entities is optically active and can be resolved into a pair of non-superimposable mirror-image enantiomers?

solution.explanationText: A complex is optically active if it lacks an improper axis of rotation (most commonly a center of inversion or a plane of symmetry). In trans-[Co(en)2Cl2]+, there is a plane of symmetry and an inversion center, making it achiral and optically inactive. In square planar complexes like cis-[Pt(NH3)2Cl2] and [Pt(en)Cl2], the molecular plane itself acts as a plane of symmetry. In cis-[Co(en)2Cl2]+, there is no plane or center of symmetry, rendering the molecule chiral and resolvable into d- and l-enantiomers.

stemText: According to Valence Bond Theory (VBT), the hybridization, geometry, and magnetic character of the complex ion [Ni(CN)4]2- are, respectively: (Atomic number of Ni = 28)

solution.explanationText: Nickel in [Ni(CN)4]2- is in the +2 oxidation state with the configuration [Ar] 3d^8. Cyanide (CN-) is a strong-field ligand that causes pairing of the two unpaired 3d electrons, vacating one 3d orbital. The central Ni2+ then undergoes dsp2 hybridization utilizing one 3d, one 4s, and two 4p orbitals. This results in a square planar geometry. Because all electrons are paired, the complex is diamagnetic.

stemText: For an octahedral coordination complex of a d5 transition metal ion, the crystal field splitting energy Delta_o is smaller than the mean pairing energy P (Delta_o < P). The ground-state electronic configuration of the metal ion in the octahedral crystal field is:

solution.explanationText: When Delta_o < P, the crystal field splitting energy is smaller than the energy required to pair two electrons in the same orbital (weak-field regime). Consequently, electrons occupy orbitals following Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity before pairing occurs: three electrons singly occupy the lower t2g orbitals, and the remaining two electrons occupy the higher eg orbitals, yielding a high-spin configuration of t2g^3 eg^2.

stemText: In homoleptic transition metal carbonyls, synergistic bonding involves sigma-donation from carbon to metal and pi back-donation from filled metal d-orbitals into empty pi* antibonding orbitals of CO. Which of the following isoelectronic carbonyl species possesses the LONGEST and WEAKEST C-O bond?

options.label: D
options.text: All three have identical C-O bond lengths because they are isoelectronic.

solution.explanationText: The three carbonyl complexes [V(CO)6]-, [Cr(CO)6], and [Mn(CO)6]+ are isoelectronic (each has a d6 metal center). The negative charge on the vanadium center in [V(CO)6]- maximizes electron density on the metal, resulting in the strongest M -> C pi back-donation into the pi* antibonding molecular orbitals of CO. Populating antibonding pi* orbitals reduces the C-O bond order most drastically, giving [V(CO)6]- the longest and weakest C-O bond.

stemText: What is the Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE, excluding pairing energy contributions) for a low-spin octahedral complex of a Co3+ ion (d6 system) where Delta_o > P?

solution.explanationText: In a low-spin octahedral complex with Delta_o > P, all 6 d-electrons pair up in the lower-energy t2g orbitals, giving the electronic configuration t2g^6 eg^0. The CFSE formula is CFSE = [-0.4 * n(t2g) + 0.6 * n(eg)] * Delta_o. Substituting n(t2g) = 6 and n(eg) = 0: CFSE = [-0.4 * 6 + 0.6 * 0] * Delta_o = -2.4 Delta_o.

stemText: In tetrahedral crystal field splitting, the d-orbitals split into two sets: lower-energy e orbitals and higher-energy t2 orbitals. Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding tetrahedral complexes?

options.label: A
options.text: The crystal field splitting Delta_t is related to octahedral splitting by Delta_t = (4/9) Delta_o for identical ligands and metal ions.

options.label: B
options.text: Tetrahedral complexes virtually always form high-spin complexes because Delta_t is significantly smaller than the pairing energy P.

options.label: C
options.text: The e orbitals (dx2-y2, dz2) point directly along the ligand approach directions in a tetrahedral field.

options.label: D
options.text: Orbital splitting in a tetrahedral field is inverted compared to that in an octahedral field.

solution.explanationText: In a tetrahedral crystal field, four ligands approach along the diagonals of a cube towards the vertices of a tetrahedron. None of the d-orbitals point directly at the incoming ligands, but the t2 orbitals (dxy, dyz, dxz) point closer to the directions of ligand approach than the e orbitals (dx2-y2, dz2). Therefore, t2 orbitals experience greater electrostatic repulsion and are raised in energy, while e orbitals are lowered. Statement C is incorrect because e orbitals do not point along the ligand directions.

Delta_t மதிப்பு இணையாக்கல் ஆற்றல் P-ஐ விடக் கணிசமாகக் குறைவு என்பதால் நான்முகி அணைவுகள் எப்போதும் உயர் சுழற்சி அணைவுகளாகவே உருவாகின்றன.

stemText: The correct IUPAC name of the anionic coordination compound K3[Fe(C2O4)3] is:

solution.explanationText: In K3[Fe(C2O4)3]: The cation is named first: 'potassium'. In the complex anion [Fe(C2O4)3]3-, three oxalate ligands are named as 'trioxalato'. Oxidation state of iron is: 3(+1) + Fe + 3(-2) = 0 => Fe - 3 = 0 => Fe = +3, denoted as (III). Because the coordination sphere carries a net negative charge, the Latin name of the metal ending in '-ate' is used: 'ferrate'. Thus, the IUPAC name is Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III).

stemText: Three octahedral cobalt(III) complexes [Co(NH3)6]3+, [Co(CN)6]3-, and [Co(H2O)6]3+ absorb visible light corresponding to d-d transitions. According to the spectrochemical series, the correct order of the wavelength of maximum absorption (lambda_max) for these three complexes is:

solution.explanationText: According to the spectrochemical series, ligand field strength increases in the order: H2O < NH3 < CN-. The crystal field splitting energy Delta_o follows the same order: Delta_o([Co(H2O)6]3+) < Delta_o([Co(NH3)6]3+) < Delta_o([Co(CN)6]3-). Because the absorbed photon energy delta E = h*c / lambda_max = Delta_o, the wavelength of absorption is inversely proportional to Delta_o (lambda_max proportional to 1 / Delta_o). Therefore, the wavelength of maximum absorption decreases as: [Co(CN)6]3- < [Co(NH3)6]3+ < [Co(H2O)6]3+.

stemText: The hexaaquacopper(II) complex ion, [Cu(H2O)6]2+, does not form a regular octahedron; instead, it displays significant tetragonal elongation where two axial Cu-O bonds are noticeably longer than the four equatorial Cu-O bonds. This phenomenon is known as the Jahn-Teller distortion and occurs primarily because:

options.label: A
options.text: The eg orbitals in high-spin d9 Cu(II) are asymmetrically (unevenly) occupied by 3 electrons (t2g^6 eg^3), breaking the electronic degeneracy.

options.label: B
options.text: Water is a strong-field chelating ligand that repels axial ligands.

options.label: C
options.text: The t2g orbitals are half-filled, causing uniform spatial repulsion.

options.label: D
options.text: Copper undergoes dsp2 planar hybridization in the presence of water.

solution.explanationText: According to the Jahn-Teller theorem, any non-linear molecular system in a degenerate electronic ground state undergoes spontaneous geometric distortion that lowers its symmetry and removes the degeneracy. In Cu(II) (3d^9), the octahedral configuration is t2g^6 eg^3. The eg doublet is unevenly occupied (either (dz2)^2 (dx2-y2)^1 or (dz2)^1 (dx2-y2)^2). Placing two electrons in dz2 provides greater screening along the z-axis, pushing the two axial ligands farther away (tetragonal elongation) and stabilizing the complex.

stemText: The overall formation constant for [Ni(NH3)6]2+ is log beta = 8.6, whereas for [Ni(en)3]2+ (where en = ethylenediamine) it is log beta = 18.3 at 298 K. The extraordinary thermodynamic stability of [Ni(en)3]2+ over [Ni(NH3)6]2+ (the chelate effect) is predominantly driven by:

options.label: B
options.text: A huge negative enthalpy change (Delta H° << 0) arising from stronger Ni-N covalent bonds in en.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: A large positive entropy change (Delta S° > 0) caused by the net release of displaced monodentate solvent molecules.

solution.explanationText: The chelate effect refers to the enhanced stability of complexes formed by polydentate chelating ligands compared to those formed by equivalent monodentate ligands. When three bidentate en molecules replace six coordinated water molecules from hydrated nickel(II): [Ni(H2O)6]2+ + 3en <=> [Ni(en)3]2+ + 6H2O, 4 reactant particles generate 7 product particles. This net increase in independent molecules in solution creates a large positive entropy change (Delta S° > 0), driving Delta G° to be much more negative.
